arr.title: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR)
arr.content:
ARR is the annualised value of active SaaS subscription contracts at period end -- the headline growth metric for a subscription software business, distinct from statutory revenue which also includes consulting and one-off implementation fees.

For TechnologyOne Limited: ARR was $554.6m at FY2025 (91% of total revenue) against management's own $1bn+ ARR target by FY30 -- roughly an 80% increase required over five years, implying ARR growth needs to stay near its historical double-digit pace. UK ARR ($51.8m, ~9% of group ARR) is the named growth lever outside the mature ANZ base.

What to watch:

  • ARR growth rate versus the FY30 target trajectory
  • UK ARR growth rate versus ANZ (is the expansion story actually accelerating?)
  • The November 2025 ~17% single-day share price fall followed a softer-than-expected ARR/NRR print despite a record result -- this metric moves the stock more than headline revenue

nrr.title: Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
nrr.content:
NRR measures revenue retained and expanded from the existing customer base over the prior year (upsell and cross-sell less downgrades and churn), excluding new-customer revenue. 100% means the existing book neither grew nor shrank.

For TechnologyOne Limited: NRR has stepped down each period disclosed -- 117% (FY2024) to 115% (FY2025) to 114% (H1 FY2026) -- against management's own stated target range of 115%-120%. It is now tracking below that range, which the market has read as an early signal on growth durability even though headline revenue still printed records.

What to watch:

  • Whether the H1 FY2026 114% is a seasonal dip or a trend break
  • NRR relative to the 115%-120% target band each period
  • NRR is FY/H1-disclosed only, not quarterly -- a short run of data, so weight the trend over any single print

recurringRevenue.title: Recurring revenue mix
recurringRevenue.content:
Recurring revenue (subscription/SaaS fees) against total revenue, which also includes consulting, implementation and other one-off fees.

For TechnologyOne Limited: recurring revenue was $553.2m of $598.5m total revenue in FY2025 (~92%) -- the completed transition from on-premise licensing to a single-instance SaaS model. A rising recurring share means future revenue is increasingly visible and contracted rather than won deal-by-deal.

What to watch:

  • The gap between recurring revenue and ARR (timing/definitional differences)
  • Consulting revenue trend -- management flags it as structurally declining as the SaaS transition completes

adjustedFcf.title: Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow (company measures)
adjustedFcf.content:
These are management's own non-IFRS measures disclosed in results commentary, adjusting for significant items. They are not the same series as the core_metrics Reported FCF (operating cash flow less CapEx) or the DCF's Owner FCF (which further strips SBC, interest income and lease principal) shown elsewhere on this dashboard.

For TechnologyOne Limited: use this chart only to track management's own cash conversion narrative against their guidance; use the Cash Flow section below for the comparable, DCF-consistent measure.

What to watch:

  • Adjusted FCF as a share of Adjusted EBITDA (cash conversion)
  • Divergence from Reported FCF elsewhere on this page -- large gaps mean the adjustments matter

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TechnologyOne Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TechnologyOne Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TechnologyOne Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TechnologyOne Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TechnologyOne Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
